newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Howard says won't make GDP forecast.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Howard says won't make GDP forecast.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Friday that he would not specifically forecast four percent growth in gross domestic product (GDP), despite endorsing a recent central bank statement that the country could aim for at least 4.5 percent.
"I'm not going to define a prediction," Howard told a reporter who asked when GDP growth would surpass four percent.
On Tuesday, Reserve Bank Governor Ian Macfarlane cited low inflationary pressures and said Australian could aim for 4.5 percent annual GDP growth or more in the next few years.
Macfarlane's outlook is far ahead of Australia's long-run trend growth rate of around 3.2 percent.
The economy has been expanding since the recession of 1990-91 but decelerated last year. GDP grew just 2.4 percent between the March quarters of 1996 and 1997.
The government's latest GDP forecast, published in the May budget, projects GDP for the year to June 1998 3.75 percent higher than the previous year's.
Underlying inflation, which excludes volatile items, was 1.7 percent in the year to the June quarter and advance indicators of consumer prices remain generally subdued.
